Replace it with hard Existence(has_key), hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal), and hard Existence(at_goal); drop the redundant hard Existence(has_key) only if the compiler's clue shows the chain already forces it — with Precedence(has_key, at_goal) plus Existence(at_goal) forcing has_key, keep just Existence(at_goal) hard and Precedence(has_key, at_goal) hard.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The task commands reaching the goal (unconditionally, no preference cue: 'get to the goal square'), but the only Existence(at_goal) is soft, and soft Existence forces nothing. The hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) does not require at_goal either, so FINAL_STATES would only be reachable... more importantly nothing makes at_goal happen. Add a hard Existence(at_goal); then it together with Precedence(has_key, at_goal) forces has_key, so the hard Existence(has_key) becomes redundant and should be removed. 'if you can' does not scope a preference here; the step onto the goal ends the episode, and the environment makes reaching it always possible.

CHANGES REQUIRED: Existence(has_key) is redundant — the compiler confirms it is already implied by Precedence(has_key, at_goal) plus Existence(at_goal). Remove it; keep the hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) and hard Existence(at_goal).

CHANGES REQUIRED: Existence(has_key) is redundant — the hard Existence(at_goal) with the hard Precedence(has_key, at_goal) already forces has_key, as the compiler's Redundant clue confirms. Remove it and keep Existence(at_goal) plus Precedence(has_key, at_goal).
